model_output.verdict: Your healthcare operations career moves from clinic management to running Lakeshore Dental Partners. The growth, margin and workforce results back up that progression. I’d want to talk to you.
write_up: Your resume is strong because it connects executive decisions to changes in the business! At Lakeshore Dental Partners, a recruiter can see both the reach of your COO role and what changed as the organization grew.

The practice growth line is a model: it names acquisitions and openings alongside the same-store margin change. The earlier roles also show a clear progression from clinics to enterprise operations, and your experience leads your education.

Your resume isn't the likely obstacle to a recruiter moving you forward. Add how you reduced appointment waits, then consider whether an enterprise-wide decision belongs in the operating plan line for CEO-level roles. Competition for those roles will also matter.

cards.line: - Reduced patient wait time to third available appointment from 21 days to 6 across primary care
cards.cannot_tell: The wait time change is substantial, but a recruiter can't see what you changed to achieve it. That decision would show how you improved access across primary care.
cards.example: Reduced patient wait time to third available appointment from 21 days to 6 across primary care by [operational change]
cards.question: What did you change to reduce the wait for an appointment?

cards.line: - Grew the practice count from 38 to 140 through 61 acquisitions and 41 de novo openings while raising same-store EBITDA margin from 17% to 23%
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as the model. It puts the ways you grew the organization next to the margin change, so the growth is more than a practice count.

cards.line: - Own the annual operating plan and the $410M P&L with the CFO
cards.cannot_tell: For a CEO-level role, an enterprise-wide decision tied to the operating plan would show more of how you set direction.
cards.example: Own the annual operating plan and the $410M P&L with the CFO; [enterprise-wide decision] shaped [business priority]
cards.question: What enterprise-wide decision did you make through the operating plan, and what priority did it shape?

cards.line: - Implemented the centralized call center that replaced 18 front-desk phone trees, cutting abandoned calls from 12% to 3%
cards.cannot_tell: Move this to the first line under the Vice President role. It shows the operating change and the reduction in abandoned calls before the clinic count.

fit.why: Your headline and current Lakeshore Dental Partners role both position you as a Chief Operating Officer in multi-site healthcare.
fit.level: executive, leads operations for 140 practices and owns the $410M P&L with the CFO
fit.note: Your experience points to executive operations roles in multi-site healthcare services. The board reporting and operating plan also give you a base for showing enterprise direction in a CEO-level search.
